note: Phase 0's deliverable text describes useKeyboard as "mounted once at the app-shell/layout level as the single global shortcut registry", but the actual mount point (frontend/apps/web/src/features/command-center/hooks/useCommandPalette.ts, invoked from CommandPalette.tsx inside CommandCenter.tsx) is only rendered on the /command-center route (see frontend/apps/web/src/app/Router.tsx's commandCenterRoute) -- NOT frontend/apps/web/src/app/Layout.tsx, which is the actual app shell wrapping every route via <Outlet/>. So Cmd+K/Ctrl+K/Escape only work while on the Command Center page; navigating to /email, /inbox-cleaner, /rules, /settings, etc. unmounts CommandPalette and the shortcut stops working entirely. This is NOT a regression introduced by this phase -- CommandPalette's mount location is unchanged; the phase only fixed a pre-existing double-registration bug that made Cmd+K silently do nothing even on /command-center (see the phase 0 commit summary). No definition_of_done line in pipeline.yml actually requires cross-route availability, so this phase reaches a green gate without resolving it. Not fixed here: moving the registration into Layout.tsx is out of phase 0's touches: allowlist (shared/hooks/**, command-center/**, email/EmailList.tsx) and is a real architecture decision (does Cmd+K become truly site-wide, or does each route register its own relevant shortcuts through the same shared useKeyboard mechanism?) that a human should make deliberately, especially since phase 1's deliverables (C/R/F shortcuts "global, not scoped to a focused email") may run into the same route-scoping question from a different route (email/chat features, not command-center) and should account for this when planning where those shortcuts actually get registered.
